clue.text: The average American can make fortune, ultimately

parts.note: can is slang for a toilet, as is john
to make is to do, as in do a cake

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word fortune

explanation.surface: An ordinary American hoping to get rich in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: JOHN is American slang for a lavatory, like 'can'.
explanation.definitionFit: The placeholder name for an unidentified or typical man in the US is this one.

clue.text: Writer's block? TV dramatist has to start afresh

indicators.note: starting afresh means the first letter is swapped for a new one

parts.note: Dennis Potter wrote television dramas such as The Singing Detective

explanation.surface: A blocked TV writer must begin again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has to start afresh' replaces the P of POTTER with a fresh first letter, J; the definition leaves that letter to the solver.
explanation.definitionFit: A notepad is literally a block of paper for a writer, punning on writer's block.

clue.text: Does it attract good luck?

parts.note: a U-shaped piece of iron that pulls metal towards it is shaped like the farrier's lucky charm, so it might be thought to draw in luck

explanation.definitionFit: A U-shaped magnet looks like the lucky iron shoe of a horse, and magnets attract.

clue.text: Drag girl around one area of Ireland

indicators.note: the drag and girl go around the word one, holding it

parts.note: D is the symbol for drag, the resisting force in aerodynamics
gal is an informal word for a girl
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drag queen and a girl tour a corner of Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: D for drag is the physics symbol for air resistance, not a cross-dresser's outfit; 'around' has the drag-and-girl pair enclose the one.
explanation.definitionFit: Donegal is a county in the north-west of the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: Fellow among the richest

indicators.note: among says the letters are found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A man counted among the wealthiest.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric is a man's name, and crosswords use any first name for a chap.

clue.text: Looks good, note, wearing ties

indicators.note: the ties wear the note, so the note sits inside them

parts.note: laces are ties, as on shoes

explanation.surface: Someone looks smart, with a note tucked into a tie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' puts N inside LACES, after G.
explanation.definitionFit: Glances are quick looks, both as plural nouns and as verbs in the third person.

clue.text: Crowd's at first totally captivated by bloodthirsty tale

indicators.note: captivated means held captive, so these letters are held inside the word for bloodthirsty

parts.note: gory means bloody, delighting in bloodshed
hosts are crowds, multitudes; read as a plural

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of totally

explanation.surface: An audience is spellbound by a violent story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crowd's' reads as a possessive but supplies a plural; 'captivated by' wraps the bloodthirsty word around the crowds plus the first letter of 'totally'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost story is a tale of the supernatural told to frighten listeners.

clue.text: Adult has endless A cardiac trouble in part of Greece

parts.note: A is the film certificate for adult

indicators.note: trouble means disturbed, so the letters are rearranged
endless removes the outer letters of the phrase A cardiac

explanation.surface: A grown-up has a heart problem in Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' strips the first and last letters from A CARDIAC, leaving CARDIA; 'trouble' rearranges that into RCADIA, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadia is a region of the Peloponnese, the pastoral paradise of legend.

clue.text: Becoming rotten, my Christmas tree stinks

indicators.note: rotten means spoilt or decayed, signalling that the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Christmas tree that has gone off and smells bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stinks' looks like the verb; it is old schoolboy slang for chemistry, and so for the teacher of it.
explanation.definitionFit: In British school slang, Stinks was the nickname for the science teacher of smelly experiments.

clue.text: Sweden's lumberjacks are hard workers

parts.note: S is the international vehicle code for Sweden
loggers fell trees for timber

explanation.surface: Swedish lumberjacks are a hard-working lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A slogger is someone who toils steadily at hard work.

clue.text: TV compere hasn't the heart to introduce popular old movie director

indicators.note: lacking the heart means the central letter of the presenter's surname is dropped

parts.note: Chris Tarrant is a British TV presenter, host of Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?
in means popular, fashionable

explanation.surface: A television host introduces a famous film-maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hasn't the heart' drops the middle letter of the presenter's surname; 'to introduce' is only a link setting the rest after it. Chris Tarrant is a well-known British TV presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: Quentin Tarantino is a film director, known for Pulp Fiction and Reservoir Dogs.

clue.text: Leader of choir wants to repeat section of Mass

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of choir

parts.note: to redo something is to repeat it

explanation.surface: A choirmaster wants to sing part of the Mass again.
explanation.definitionFit: The Creed, the statement of belief beginning 'I believe', is a sung part of the Mass.

clue.text: Though retired, say, engineers come out into the open

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: e.g., for example, is what 'say' means in 'say, a dog'
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Retired engineers, say, still venture out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Though retired' turns the whole run EGREME around. REME, the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, is a British Army corps; engineers are more often RE in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge is to appear or come out from hiding.

clue.text: Carefully watching Stuart Little coming to an end

indicators.note: little means the name is cut short to its familiar form

parts.note: dying means coming to an end, as a fire does

explanation.surface: Stuart Little, the children's mouse, is nearing his end.
explanation.walkthrough: Stuart Little is a fictional mouse, but here 'Little' shortens Stuart to STU.
explanation.definitionFit: Studying means examining closely, observing with care.

clue.text: Establish permanent home in Yorkshire town U W overlooking hill

indicators.note: in a down clue, the town sits above, looking over, the hill

parts.note: Settle is a market town in North Yorkshire
a down is a rolling hill

explanation.surface: Moving to a Yorkshire town with a view of the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: Settle is a small market town in the Yorkshire Dales.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle down is to adopt a stable life in one place.

clue.text: Briefly the accelerator's going wrong in this gas-guzzling vehicle

indicators.note: going wrong signals that these letters are jumbled up
briefly means cut short, so the word the loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive s included as a letter

explanation.surface: A big car's accelerator is broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' trims THE to TH, then 'going wrong' rearranges TH plus ACCELERATORS. A CHELSEA TRACTOR is British slang for a big 4x4 driven in the city; Chelsea is a wealthy London district.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase mocks four-wheel-drive SUVs that burn fuel on school runs in posh urban areas.

clue.text: Stores vegetable E D S broth to consume bit NUR S E S by bit

parts.note: stock is a broth made by simmering vegetables or bones

parts.words: consume bit NUR S E S by bit
parts.note: to sup is to take liquid in small mouthfuls

explanation.surface: Laying in a store of vegetable soup to sip slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: To stock up is to lay in supplies, so 'stores' as a verb.

clue.text: Male is given part in this young Conservative's play

indicators.note: the male is given a part inside the word this, so it goes inside

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
a Tory boy is a young Conservative, with the s of the possessive

explanation.surface: A man is cast in a young Tory's stage play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is given part in' sets the male pronoun inside 'this'. 'Tory boy' is British slang for a young Conservative party member; the play is by Alan Bennett.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Bennett wrote this stage work about grammar-school pupils preparing for Oxbridge.

clue.text: Guess silver can be located in one underground source

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the silver is located inside the underground source

parts.note: a mine is an underground source of ore
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Guessing where silver might be found underground.
explanation.definitionFit: To imagine is to suppose or conjecture, as in 'I imagine so'.

clue.text: What might be inhibiting, principally, among beauty contest participants?

definitions.text: What might be inhibiting, principally, among beauty contest participants?

indicators.note: among places that letter inside the beauty queens

parts.note: belles are beautiful women

indicators.note: principally takes the first, principal letter of inhibiting

explanation.surface: Beauty queens hold their stomachs in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' puts I inside BELLES. As a whole, the clue describes tummies the contestants hold in.
explanation.definitionFit: Contestants pull in their stomachs to look slim, so these are what they hold in.

clue.text: Bird dog perhaps on lake

parts.note: a dog is an example of a pet
re means on or about, as in a letter heading
L is short for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A gun dog flushes a bird on the lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird dog' suggests a gun dog, but 'Bird' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The petrel is a seabird that skims low over the waves.

clue.text: Scare had disrupted game

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fright broke up the party game.
explanation.definitionFit: Charades is a party game of miming words for others to guess.

clue.text: Dance initially banned by church in part of France

indicators.note: the first letter of the dance is banned, removed

parts.note: the salsa is a Latin dance
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: The church forbade dancing in a French region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially banned' drops the S of SALSA, leaving ALSA.
explanation.definitionFit: Alsace is a region in north-eastern France, on the German border.

clue.text: Maybe sex attracts them

parts.note: it is a coy word for sex appeal or sex itself
'em is a casual short form of them

explanation.surface: Perhaps lovers are drawn by desire.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a couple are drawn together by sex, maybe.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantic couple is called an item, and attraction brings them together.

clue.text: Wrong road on mountain

parts.note: a sin is a wrong
the A1 is the main road from London to Edinburgh, written AI with the numeral as a letter

explanation.surface: Taking the wrong road on a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is Britain's longest numbered road; its 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Sinai is the peak where Moses received the Ten Commandments.

clue.text: Unfashionable titfer designed by him?

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion

indicators.note: designed means shaped anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned hat made by a clothier.
explanation.walkthrough: A titfer is Cockney rhyming slang for a hat (tit for tat); 'designed' rearranges its letters. The whole clue is the definition: such a supplier might make a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothes supplier provides garments, so a hat could well be made by such a tradesman.

clue.text: Sales pitch to attract new order

parts.note: patter is a salesman's glib talk

explanation.surface: A salesman's spiel tries to draw in a fresh order.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern is a regular arrangement or design, an order things follow.

clue.text: Strong wind and fog associated with central part of Urals

parts.note: mist is a thin fog

indicators.note: the central part is the word Urals without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A gale and fog sweep the Ural mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: The mistral is a cold northerly wind blowing down the Rhone valley into southern France.
